latest_nl_proof:
Let n > 1 be fixed, and define F_n(x) = floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k. We prove that F_n(x+z) = F_n(x) for every real x and every integer z.

Since z is an integer, for any real t we have floor(t+z) = floor(t) + z. Applying this with t = nx and t = kx gives

floor(n(x+z)) = floor(nx+nz) = floor(nx) + nz,

and for each k = 1, ..., n,

floor(k(x+z)) = floor(kx+kz) = floor(kx) + kz.

Therefore

sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+z))/k = sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)+kz)/k
= sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + sum_{k=1}^n z
= sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nz.

Substituting into the definition of F_n gives

F_n(x+z) = floor(n(x+z)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+z))/k
= (floor(nx)+nz) - (sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nz)
= floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
= F_n(x).

Hence F_n is periodic with period 1, so the stated identity holds for all real x and all integers z.
